--- docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
+++ docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
@@ -198,13 +198,15 @@
 Under `/v1/{tenant}/`. Operator token unless marked.
 
 With `AUTH_MODE=enforced`, diagnostic reads (lift, rows, history, slots, exploration, day/window reports and brand discovery) require an operator token explicitly granted the selected tenant; a site key alone is insufficient. Open/unset mode retains the existing demo read policy.
 
-Enforced-mode recent/receipt, ledger-by-ID, replay, batch-list and erasure-list reads (including HEAD) require acknowledged D1 audit admission before data access and a correlated result before response release. Result status records the handler's HTTP status, not client delivery or completed erasure. Missing audit storage/schema/key or failed acknowledgement returns sanitized, no-store 503. These reads require local migration `0011_operator_audit_tenant.sql` and explicit nonblank `IDENTITY_SALT`; deployment is a separate step. Audit rows retain the authenticated actor, tenant, fixed operation/route, server time/request ID and keyed, tenant-separated selector references; validated by-ID/replay subjects also receive a keyed result reference. Actor IDs over 200 or record selectors over 2048 characters are refused, never truncated. References remain subject-related, not anonymous. No raw subject/record IDs, paths, queries, bodies or emails are logged in this schema. Tenant-wide listings do not audit each constituent or subsequent external downloads. Open/demo reads remain unaudited; identity and mutation auditing, historical completeness, retention and key-lifecycle policy remain separate work.
+Enforced-mode recent/receipt, ledger-by-ID, replay, batch-list and erasure-list reads (including HEAD) require acknowledged D1 audit admission before data access and a correlated result before response release. Result status records the handler's HTTP status, not client delivery or completed erasure. Missing audit storage/schema/key or failed acknowledgement returns sanitized, no-store 503. These reads require local migration `0011_operator_audit_tenant.sql` and explicit nonblank `IDENTITY_SALT`; deployment is a separate step. Audit rows retain the authenticated actor, tenant, fixed operation/route, server time/request ID and keyed, tenant-separated selector references; validated by-ID/replay subjects also receive a keyed result reference. Actor IDs over 200 or record selectors over 2048 characters are refused, never truncated. References remain subject-related, not anonymous. No raw subject/record IDs, paths, queries, bodies or emails are logged in this schema. Tenant-wide listings do not audit each constituent or subsequent external downloads. Open/demo reads remain unaudited; other identity/mutation operations, historical completeness, retention and key-lifecycle policy remain separate work.
 
+Identity visitor/shopper GETs (including HEAD), identity resolve/erase, ledger erase and ledger rewrite also require acknowledged audit admission/result in enforced mode. They add minimized `subject_operation` v2 records to the same tenant-admin audit view; existing v1 read records remain readable. Resolve validates the entire ≤1MiB request with1–1000 nonblank accounts of normalized length≤200, retaining original response keys and trimmed identity semantics without filtering/truncation. Every account ordinal has a keyed account reference and, on success, its actual mapped shopper reference. Ten-member chunks stay≤2048 UTF-8 bytes each and the whole phase≤512KiB; one atomic D1 statement per phase means two audit write queries even for1000 accounts. Audit actor is the current caller, not a previous erasure job's retained actor. Identity `local_complete` still has `complete:false`; ledger ring failures/unbound hosts and rewrite `more`/`remaining` counters are recorded as returned, never full deletion. After an erasure command enters its mutation callback, a thrown/invalid receipt or failed result acknowledgement yields sanitized503 with server `requestId`, `outcome:outcome_unknown`, `operationMayHaveApplied:true` and `auditStatus` (`recorded`, or `unconfirmed` when acknowledgement failed). This does not imply rollback or safe automatic replay. Admission refusal starts no target operation. Historical import audit, external downloads, per-subject proof of bulk rewrites, retention/key lifecycle and full erasure remain separate; valid open/demo operations remain unaudited.
+
 | Route | Does |
 |---|---|
-| `GET audit[?limit=1..100&before=id]` | Minimized tenant read-audit entries in descending ID order, default 50; returned `before` is the next keyset cursor or null. Requires both an explicit tenant grant and the existing admin role in every mode; no-store. Its own read has one admission/result pair. Legacy global rows retain null tenant and are excluded, not assigned an inferred tenant; the legacy global audit view excludes these new subject-read rows |
+| `GET audit[?limit=1..100&before=id]` | Minimized tenant subject-read/operation audit entries in descending ID order, default 50; returned `before` is the next keyset cursor or null. Requires both an explicit tenant grant and the existing admin role in every mode; no-store. Its own read has one admission/result pair. Legacy global rows retain null tenant and are excluded, not assigned an inferred tenant; the legacy global audit view excludes these subject-read/operation rows |
 | `GET lift?slot=&brand=[&version=]` | The slot's lift snapshot in force, or an archived version: every item's estimate in every cell. Operator token |
 | `GET lift/history?slot=&brand=` | Every archived snapshot version for the slot |
 | `GET lift/rows?slot=&brand=[&level=pooled\|cells][&item=][&q=][&sort=][&dir=][&limit=][&cursor=]` | The grid one page at a time, cut by the server: one pooled row per item, or one item's cells (`level=cells&item=`), filtered by `q` over the item id, your id, the title and the cell, sorted by any column, fifty a page up to five hundred. `total` counts what matched; `cursor` fetches the next page and is bound to the snapshot version, so a listing that outlives a publish answers 409 and starts again. Names and a merchandiser's freeze or reject ride each row. Operator token |
 | `GET brands` | In enforced mode, only the operator's explicitly granted brands in manifest order, preserving each brand's original default flag: the application's brand picker |
